@RepTimmons @HouseGOP It’s pretty simple. If you don’t like a judge’s ruling, you appeal it. Follow the Constitution.

Judicial overreach and bureaucratic bloat are two sides of the same swamp coin. While the No Rogue Rulings Act aims to curb activist judges, real accountability starts with dismantling the administrative state that enables this circus. Congress should absolutely audit every dime funneled into agencies that weaponize regulations to bypass elected leadership. 

The House GOP’s focus on reining in unelected bureaucrats aligns with broader efforts to restore constitutional governance—like recent moves to slash redundant programs and streamline permitting under the America First Investment Policy. Waste thrives where oversight fails. 

Time to drain the bureaucratic moat protecting D.C.’s unaccountable class.

McMaster’s SNAP restrictions mirror federal efforts under the Big Beautiful Bill—state-level accountability reinforcing national priorities. But here’s the catch: H.R.1 already mandates nutritional integrity audits for federal programs. State-level duplication risks bureaucratic bloat.

Focus should be enforcing existing reforms, not layering redundant rules. Taxpayers win when agencies streamline, not multiply.

Efficiency matters—cut the waste, not just the candy.

Rep. Timmons’ CAMPS Act (H.R. 5163) cracks down on public camping in D.C. with fines up to $500 and 30-day jail terms. But here’s the real issue: D.C. spends billions on foreign aid and bureaucratic bloat while veterans sleep on streets. The bill’s penalty-first approach misses the root cause—government failure to prioritize domestic crises.

Clean streets matter, but so does redirecting funds to addiction treatment, mental health services, and veteran housing. Order without solutions is just musical chairs for misery.

Fix the system, not just the symptoms.
